## Thankful for Our Players: A Thanksgiving Note to the Skillz Community


- by Skillz
- Nov. 13, 2026
- 3 min read


-
-
-
-


Thanksgiving is a time to slow down and say thank you to the people who make the year better. For us at Skillz, that list starts with you, our players.


Every match you play, every tournament you enter, and every comment you leave in our community helps make Skillz a home for skill-based competition. This week, we want to take a moment to say thanks and share a few easy ways to make room for play over the holiday.


## **What We’re Thankful For This Year**


- **Your competitive spirit.** You show up ready to play your best, whether it’s a quick word search on a lunch break or a longer puzzle session on a Sunday afternoon.


- **Our Facebook community.** The tips, celebrations, and friendly rivalries you share in the Skillz Facebook community remind us why we build what we build.


- **Your stories.** Players have told us how they found a favorite game, picked up a new strategy, or turned a casual habit into a competitive routine. We love hearing them, and we’ve been proud to share some of them on this blog.


- **Your feedback.** Every suggestion helps us make the experience better for everyone who plays.


## **Make Room for Play This Thanksgiving**


The holiday is about family, food, and football, but there’s usually a quiet moment or two in between. Here are a few natural times to fit in a match.


- **While the turkey’s in the oven.** A round of Ball Sort: Real Cash or Word Search Real Cash Tournaments fits neatly between kitchen tasks.


- **At halftime.** A head-to-head match of Speed Pool keeps the competitive energy going between quarters.


- **After dinner.** When everyone settles onto the couch, a round of Sushi Drop or Golf Blitz 3D makes an easy way to wind down.


- **Over the long weekend.** With a few extra days off, it’s a good time to try a Skillz game you haven’t played yet, like Number Shoot Tournament.


## **Turn Family Time Into Friendly Competition**


Thanksgiving brings together people of every age and gaming background. That makes it a great time to introduce someone to the games you love.


- **Start with a practice game.** Practice lets new players learn the rules and get comfortable with the controls with nothing on the line.


- **Pick a classic.** Games built on familiar classics, like Blackout Poker and Speed Pool, are easy for most families to pick up.


- **Compare results.** Playing the same game and comparing how you did is a simple way to bring some friendly rivalry to the table.


Not sure where a new player should start? Our guide to finding a Skillz game that fits your play style is a good place to begin.


## **Keep It Fun**


The holidays are about the people around you. Decide ahead of time how long you want to play, take breaks, and keep games a fun part of the day rather than the center of it.


## **Share What You’re Thankful For**


We’d love to hear from you. Head over to the Skillz Facebook community and tell us what you’re thankful for this year, or share your favorite holiday gaming moment. We may feature some of our favorites in a future Player Spotlight.


From all of us at Skillz, happy Thanksgiving, and thank you for playing with us.
